title: Phased deployment matrix + rollback orchestration for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Create a deterministic, auditable phased-deployment matrix and the orchestration tooling to safely promote model/runtime versions through LTS and non-LTS channels for the Hosted API. This ticket defines the policy, automated traffic-shift controller, and rollback choreography we will run for blue/green and regional rollouts, plus the operational runbook and tests required for release acceptance.
background: We currently rely on ad-hoc canaries and manual traffic shifts for major runtime/model upgrades. Incidents in Q4 revealed gaps around cache warmup, cross-region cutoff timing, and user-affinity while shifting traffic. We need a repeatable matrix that encodes: channel (canary/stable/LTS), region sequencing, traffic slope rules, health gates, and an automated rollback orchestration tied to observable signals.
design_decisions: 1) Phased Deployment Matrix: represent rollouts as a list of axes (channel, region-group, percent-schedule, warmup strategy) so we can reason about every permutation. 2) Slope-based Traffic Ramping: avoid sudden jumps by using slope parameters (tokens/sec or %/minute) instead of fixed percent steps; this smooths KV-cache pressure and GC spikes. 3) Epoch Pinning: introduce immutable epoch tokens in request headers for LTS releases to maintain affinity during multi-step rollouts and allow targeted fallbacks. 4) Rollback Orchestration: implement automated rollback triggers that can operate per-region and per-channel independently, with a two-stage rollback (fast immediate partial rollback to last known-good, then gradual drain of remaining traffic). 5) Observable-first gates: gates are defined by an expression language that references latency P99, error budget burn, model quality regressions (from synthetic evals), and customer-facing error rate thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Canary (internal only) — 1 AZ in primary region, slope 2%/min up to 5%, 30m hold. Phase B: Regional ramp — add secondary regions sequentially with slope 1%/min, KV-cache warmup window 45m per region. Phase C: Cross-region steady-state — move to stable channel with 25% traffic, 6h observation window, enable LTS promotion window. Phase D: LTS promotion — during scheduled maintenance window with epoch pinning and DNS TTL coordination. Each step has automated pre-checks (schema compatibility, runtime health) and post-checks (synthetic evals, SLOs, cost anomalies).
metrics_and_gates: Primary signals: request success rate (5xx/4xx broken out), P50/P95/P99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, synthetic-eval quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-specific metrics), error budget burn rate. Gates are expressed in a declarative policy: e.g., `if P99 > baseline*1.35 OR synthetic_delta < -0.02 OR 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m => trigger rollback`. Maintain an allowlist for transient infra alerts to avoid noisy rollbacks.
automation_and_tools: - Traffic Scheduler Service: new controller that reads phased-deployment matrix and issues weighted routing updates via our routing API. Supports slope ramps, per-region overrides, and epoch tokens. - Rollback Engine: subscribes to telemetry streams and evaluates gate expressions; can fully automate rollback or create an incident with suggested actions depending on policy. - Release CLI: `redwood release promote|abort|status` to interact with matrices, preview routing changes, and simulate slope. - Guardrails: dry-run mode, simulated warmup checks, and a safety kill-switch that immediately reverts all traffic to the previous LTS.
runbook_and_playbooks: Operator steps for a failed gate: 1) Identify affected region(s) from alert dashboard. 2) Inspect synthetic-eval run associated with the change. 3) Execute `redwood release abort --region=<r>` or allow automated rollback. 4) If partial rollback succeeds, run `redwood release drain` to migrate the remaining sessions. 5) Open postmortem with traffic-shift traces and attach PRs and deploy artifacts. Include checklist for customer communication and for Dedicated customers with pinned capacity.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for policy parser and slope math. 2) Integration in staging with a mirrored traffic generator that simulates production session stickiness. 3) Chaos scenarios: region failover during slope, cache cold-start storm, and synthetic-eval regressions. 4) Load tests to validate slope limits prevent resource oversubscription. 5) Pilot release on a low-impact tenant before broad rollout. Tests recorded in CI and tagged `release-automation`.
acceptance_criteria: - Deployment matrix format accepted and documented in Confluence. - Traffic Scheduler deployed to staging and used for 3 internal canaries without manual intervention. - Rollback Engine correctly triggers an automated rollback in at least 2 failure scenarios (synthetic regression, latency spike) in test harness. - Observability dashboards have derived metrics (slope progress, epoch affinity) and an automated post-release report. - Security review sign-off completed for epoch header mechanics and routing API changes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Slope too conservative can prolong exposure; mitigate by tuning slope per workload profile. Risk: Epoch pinning could break cached tokens for existing clients; mitigate with staged header rollout and fallback header. Risk: Automated rollback noise; mitigate with hysteresis and require two independent signals for high-impact rollbacks. Risk: Regional DNS TTLs causing lag; mitigate by coordinating TTL windows and using route affinity tokens.
notes: Prefer additive changes to routing API to avoid touching legacy flows. Coordinate with Console team for new dashboard tiles and with Solutions Eng for early adopter tenants. Postpone LTS promotion automation for non-critical model families until we validate epoch mechanics.
